title: One copy changes
hook: Track a small population through one event.

knows: An allele is a variant of a gene.
doesNotKnow: Mutation can introduce or change an allele. This model specifies one event; it does not claim mutations always occur in the same direction.

misconception: Population size and allele frequency always change together.
objective: Count allele frequency in a finite haploid population after a specified event.

claims.text: Question, stage and explanation: In a haploid model, each dot is one individual with one A or a allele. Start with 7 A and 1 a. One A allele changes to a in a single individual; the population size stays fixed. What fraction of the resulting group carries A? The resulting group has 6 A and 2 a, so its A frequency is 6 out of 8. Mutation can introduce or change an allele. This model specifies one event; it does not claim mutations always occur in the same direction. The diagram fixes this one outcome rather than predicting every real population.
claims.source: Specified finite population; biological context: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/19-1-population-evolution

claims.text: Each dot stands for one haploid individual with one allele at this locus; colours do not imply actual organism colours.
Recall: If a haploid group has 6 A individuals and 2 a individuals, what fraction carry A? There are 8 individuals and 6 carry A.
claims.source: Finite count defined by the question.

recall.question: If a haploid group has 6 A individuals and 2 a individuals, what fraction carry A?
recall.why: There are 8 individuals and 6 carry A.
